unsupervised-learning.name: Unsupervised Learning
unsupervised-learning.bio: Podcast: Ep 90: AI Pioneer Jürgen Schmidhuber on the State of AI Today

html_en:
The AI ecosystem is fracturing in productive ways — frontier models keep defying commoditization predictions, a new wave of vertical tools is reshaping how real work gets done, and the debate over what intelligence actually means is getting sharper by the day.

🧠 The Model Layer Refuses to Die

Every year, the conventional wisdom holds that foundation models are becoming commodities. Every year, it's wrong. Matt Turck put it with characteristic brevity:

2024: "The model layer is commodotizing"
2025: "The model layer is commodotizing"
2026: "The model layer is commodotizing"

The model layer: still not commodotized.

Case in point: Vercel's internal cybersecurity evals, shared by Guillermo Rauch, reveal a surprisingly differentiated field. His findings on Kimi K3, Sol, and Anthropic's new Fable model paint a picture of genuine divergence in capability — not convergence:

▪️ Kimi K3 is top-tier at cybersecurity — there is chatter on X that Moonshot benchmark-overfit. These are stealth evals. Model has raw IQ.
▪️ Sol is a leap ahead in cyber capability — at a significantly higher cost, but quite remarkable still.
▪️ Fable refuses everything — we couldn't get it to complete the run at all. — @rauchg

That last data point is striking. Anthropic's Fable — launched after what Tom Brown described as a "heroic effort by many people at Anthropic working sometimes literally around the clock" — appears to be the most safety-constrained frontier model yet, to the point of being operationally useless for even defensive security work. Whether that's a feature or a bug depends entirely on your threat model.

Meanwhile, Aaron Levie makes the geopolitical case that America's answer to Chinese model competitiveness cannot be gatekeeping:

It's fairly obvious that gate keeping models will not work at scale. Competing in AI is too economically and strategically important for China at this point, and we've now crossed the rubicon where it's clear that they can compete at near frontier levels. If this were even just 1 month ago and we saw Kimi K3 our brains would be broken. — @levie

🏢 The Enterprise Adoption Problem Has a Name

Everyone agrees enterprise AI adoption is slower than the hype suggests. Zara Zhang has identified the precise fault line with elegant economy:

The biggest barrier for enterprise AI adoption: the people who understand AI don't understand the business, and the people who understand the business don't understand AI. — @zarazhangrui

Levie, for his part, is bullish that a sprawling ecosystem is emerging to bridge exactly this gap — not just frontier labs, but applied AI companies, vertical specialists, new infrastructure layers, and professional services firms that can drive the unglamorous change management work inside large organizations. His full breakdown reads like a venture landscape map: five categories of companies all building in parallel, with no single winner yet in sight. "Way too early to call the winning architectures," he writes, "and in reality it's going to be a heterogenous environment as all other tech markets have become."

Zhang also offers a practical corrective to benchmark obsession — one worth pinning above every AI procurement desk:

Everyone should develop their "personal eval set" for AI models: a few tasks that are actually relevant to your day-to-day work/life. The industry benchmarks help but they might not reflect what will make it actually useful to you. — @zarazhangrui

🛠️ ChatGPT Work Is Turning Executives Into Dictators (of the Voice Kind)

OpenAI's ChatGPT Work rollout is generating genuine excitement among power users — not for flashy demos, but for mundane workflow takeover. Thomas Sottiaux shared a remarkably candid admission — "My job is basically delegating to ChatGPT Work now" — and then backed it up with a verbatim dictation transcript that's worth reading in full. He voice-commanded the tool to crawl thousands of Twitter DMs, extract applicants for an early-access beta, build a categorized spreadsheet with a custom taxonomy of 8–12 profession labels, and rate each applicant's AI sophistication level. The whole instruction took under two minutes to speak aloud.

It's a glimpse of what "ambient computing" actually looks like in practice — not a sci-fi interface, but a tired executive dictating to an AI assistant while probably still in pajamas. Peter Yang offered a warmer example: he and his 8-year-old daughter built a multiplication-table learning game using ChatGPT Images for the UI and animal characters, complete with a timed boss level. Consumer and enterprise use cases are converging faster than the product teams can keep up.

🤖 What Does "Intelligence" Even Mean? Schmidhuber Weighs In

Watch/Listen: Ep 90: AI Pioneer Jürgen Schmidhuber on the State of AI Today — Unsupervised Learning

The godfather of LSTMs and self-referential learning systems sat down with Unsupervised Learning for one of the more historically grounded AI conversations you'll find right now. Jürgen Schmidhuber's core thesis: we've built remarkably capable screen-bound intelligence, but "true AI" requires physical embodiment that we remain far from achieving.

"True AI is not just the AI behind the screen, which is working very well and which is passing the Turing test now. True AI is also real robots, real machinery outside of the screen and the real world and the physical world, and that's not working as well... you can't have AGI without hardware like that. You can't have AGI just behind the screen."

On the current CapEx boom, Schmidhuber is bearish on the companies while bullish on the technology — warning of a potential stock market correction even as he remains confident in long-run AI progress. And on recursive self-improvement as a moat, he's skeptical: today's RSI systems are essentially "scaled back versions, toned down versions of the Gödel machine of 2003," he argues, suggesting the labs haven't crossed any fundamental threshold that would entrench their advantage permanently.

It's a useful corrective to the triumphalism of the moment — from someone who was doing this work before most AI executives were born.

💬 The Human Premium

Rauch closed his feed with a meditation that cuts against both AI doom and AI hype in equal measure — and it's the kind of thing that lands differently coming from the CEO of a major infrastructure company than from a philosopher:

"The term 'AGI' has aged very poorly. AI can't possibly be more different from human intelligence. It's far better than human intelligence, for most economically-relevant tasks. But that doesn't make AIs better than humanity... AIs can replace tasks you do, but they can't replace the proverbial you. This is why they horribly suck at writing! Even when given a corpus of your writing and 200 Skills and 50 subagents running in gRaPh LoOps, they produce robotic prose… because they are robots." — @rauchg

Meanwhile, Swyx is tracking a more quantitative signal of the human premium in AI: he projects that Answer Engine Optimization — being findable inside AI-generated responses rather than just Google — will be "fully responsible for $1M in my revenue next year." The attention economy is being rewired, and the people who understand the new plumbing earliest will capture disproportionate value. Whether that's a reason for optimism or anxiety probably depends on which side of the knowledge gap you're on.
html_zh:
当 ChatGPT Work 重新定义"委托"的含义，AI 生态系统的价值分配之争也在悄然改变格局——今天的讨论，既关乎工具，也关乎权力。

🤖 ChatGPT Work：语音指挥一切的新工作方式

本周最引人注目的产品讨论，围绕 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT Work 展开。@thsottiaux 的一条推文迅速成为病毒式传播的案例——他直接对着手机口述了一段复杂指令，要求 ChatGPT Work 扫描他 Twitter 上数千条私信、筛选报名者、分类职业背景、并打出"AI 使用成熟度"评分，最终输出一份完整电子表格。

"我的工作基本上就是把事情委托给 ChatGPT Work。停不下来用语音指令，让它做所有事情。" —— @thsottiaux

这不是演示，这是真实工作流。与此同时，@petergyang 和他 8 岁的女儿用 ChatGPT 生成 UI 图像、配乐，搭建了一个乘法表学习游戏网站。两个案例都指向同一个趋势：AI 工具正在把"创造"和"执行"之间的门槛，降低到几乎为零。

🌐 生态系统的扩散：没有人能独吞这块蛋糕

Box 的 CEO Aaron Levie 发布了一篇罕见的长文推文，系统梳理了当前 AI 生态的分层结构。他的核心论断：AI 的价值不会只聚集在少数几家前沿实验室，而是将通过层层分发，渗透进经济的每个角落。

"现在有一个令人惊叹的生态系统正在形成，通过多种方式将 AI 扩散到现实世界……现在断言谁会赢得这场架构之战，还为时过早。现实将是一个异质化的环境，就像所有其他技术市场最终呈现的那样。" —— @levie

他列出的生态层级包括：企业定制模型服务商、垂直领域应用公司（法律、医疗、金融）、新型 AI 基础设施（编排、治理、数据安全），以及专门推动企业内部变革管理的服务公司。

Matt Turck 则以一贯的简洁风格，对"模型层将商品化"这一反复出现的预言发出了辛辣的嘲讽：

"2024年：'模型层正在商品化。'
2025年：'模型层正在商品化。'
2026年：'模型层正在商品化。'

模型层：依然没有商品化。" —— @mattturck

🛡️ Fable 的诞生与网络安全能力的前沿角力

Anthropic 本周发布了新模型 Fable，据内部人士透露，这是一次"几乎赶不上"的发布。

"这是 Anthropic 许多人有时几乎不分昼夜努力的结果……非常为所有让这一切成真的人感到骄傲。" —— @trq212

然而，Vercel 的 CEO Guillermo Rauch 随即公布了一份内部网络安全评测结果，结论颇具争议：Fable 在安全评测中拒绝了所有任务，而中国模型 Kimi K3 表现出极强的原始能力，其自研模型 Sol 则在进攻性与防御性任务之间找到了更务实的平衡。

"Fable 拒绝了所有内容——我们根本无法让它完成测试。相比之下，Sol 更愿意协助防御性网络加固……前沿级别的开源网络安全能力，已经到来。" —— @rauchg

这引出了一个尖锐问题：过于保守的安全护栏，究竟是在保护用户，还是在把防御工具让给了对手？

🧠 AI 先驱 Schmidhuber：AGI 还缺一副好手

Watch/Listen: Ep 90: AI Pioneer Jürgen Schmidhuber on the State of AI Today — Unsupervised Learning

在这期播客中，被《纽约时报》称为"AI 之父"的 Jürgen Schmidhuber 泼了一盆冷水——但方向出人意料。他对 AI 技术本身保持乐观，却对当前的资本热潮和模型公司的护城河持深度怀疑。

"真正的 AI 不只是屏幕后面的 AI……真正的 AI 还包括真实的机器人、真实的机器，在现实世界和物理世界中运作。而那部分还没有运作得很好。" —— Jürgen Schmidhuber

他的核心观点：没有能匹敌人类身体的硬件，就无法实现真正的 AGI。当前的"递归自我改进"热潮，不过是他 1992 年研究的缩水版本。至于 AI 安全，他比大多数同行要淡定得多——这与当前主流的焦虑叙事形成了鲜明对比。

💬 今日值得思考的两句话

Zara Zhang 给出了企业 AI 落地困境最精准的诊断：

"企业 AI 采用的最大障碍：懂 AI 的人不懂业务，懂业务的人不懂 AI。" —— @zarazhangrui

而 Guillermo Rauch 则对"AGI"这个词本身发出了挑战——他认为"超级智能"才是更准确的表达，但同时警告：

"AI 可以替代你做的事，但它无法替代作为独立个体的你。这就是为什么它在写作上糟透了——即便给了它你所有的文字语料、200 个技能和 50 个子代理……它们写出的是机器人的文章，因为它们就是机器人。" —— @rauchg

在一个越来越多人把写作、思考、决策都"外包"给 AI 的时代，这或许是今天最值得回味的一句话。
